Random rules & model limits

These are exploration weights, not measured planet frequencies. A class can repeat with different conditions.

Rocky climates: nitrogen-rich air and the planet tool’s terrain. Random sunlight is 1050–1500 W/m²; CO₂ is 100–900 ppm, conditional on sunlight; rotation is 0.8–3 Earth days. Stronger sunlight lowers the CO₂ ceiling. Manual ExoPlaSim bounds remain 800–1800 W/m², 10–2000 ppm and 0.5–10 days.

Extreme surfaces: atmosphere, sunlight, pressure and albedo are linked. Cold gas is screened for condensation; steam stays above 650 K; molten worlds need a dayside maximum above 1700 K. These are approximate screens, not validated phase boundaries.

All random choices have a field model. Some manually chosen gas combinations remain appearance-only. For extreme estimates, the day length is a thermal smoothing parameter, not a solved orbit. Run length applies only to ExoPlaSim; extreme estimates have no elapsed simulation time.

Model & limitations

Experimental browser port of ExoPlaSim’s Fortran model. RFL terrestrial geography, seasonal sunlight, one CPU worker. Climate always uses the original 64 × 32 grid. High display resolution adds visual detail; elevation is smoothed by the spectral model. The oversized cloud shell is an artistic projection, not a modeled cloud altitude. The model starts from an unequilibrated atmosphere; short runs show weather spin-up, not a settled climate.

Keep the tab open while running. Large runs take time, especially on a phone. This spherical model does not simulate a Banks Orbital.

CLOUD APPEARANCE

Interpretation & sources

Cloud decks follow your layer reference. Thicknesses and the intervening hydrogen envelope are compressed to make the cutaway readable. These are artistic appearance controls, not a simulation of pressure, chemistry or heat transport.

Both polar polygons continue through the water clouds as requested; their continuity at depth is speculative. The northern hexagon and the recently reported southern decagon are observed atmospheric patterns.

The water-cloud deck is rendered as glass. Metallic hydrogen is represented by a central mirror sphere; in Saturn it is a fluid envelope around a heavier interior, which this view omits.

The deeper deck’s false colors follow Cassini’s infrared image: red thermal emission, green haze and blue rings. They are not natural colors or a literal photo of one isolated cloud layer.

Physics & numerical limits

The actual MagIC Fortran solver runs in a background worker: anelastic convection, Coriolis force, entropy transport, and a polytropic density profile. At zero stratification it uses the Boussinesq limit.

Both shell boundaries are stress-free and impermeable, with fixed entropy. This experiment has no magnetic field, radiative transfer, condensation, or cloud microphysics. Cloud colors are an artistic rendering of entropy variations.

These small grids are for exploration. Strong forcing, low Ekman numbers and thin or strongly stratified shells may be under-resolved. Finer resolution and convergence studies are needed for scientific use.

Time is in d²/ν, velocity in ν/d, and entropy is dimensionless. Here d is shell thickness and ν is kinematic viscosity. Colors do not imply a measured temperature or cloud species.

POLAR STORMS

Polygonal polar vortices.

Two dimensionless numbers decide how many sides a polar storm grows.

Or click and drag the point on the regime map. Ro = U/(fL) and E = ν/(fL²), with f = 2Ω at the pole and L the jet’s distance from it.

Derive Ro & E from a world

Eddy viscosity is an order-of-magnitude free parameter; no measured value exists for any giant planet.

Interpretation & sources

The onset fit Ro = 27·E^0.72 and the wavenumber range m = 2–8 come from rotating-tank experiments on polygonal shear-layer vortices — the laboratory lineage behind the Saturn-hexagon analogue of Barbosa Aguiar et al. (2010). Band boundaries here are digitized approximations of the published regime diagram, not separate fits.

Below E = 10⁻⁵ the diagram is extrapolated: it assumes the m ∝ E^(−1/4) layer-thinning trend persists, with m capped at 10. The dotted rectangle marks the parameter region the tank experiments actually covered.

Both polar views are appearance models — prescribed kinematics, not a fluid solution. The chaotic wedge is drawn as an irregular m = 3 meander by license. As a check, Saturn’s north polar jet (10.7 h rotation, 100 m/s at 12° colatitude, ν = 10⁶ m²/s) lands on m = 6 — the observed hexagon.

About the atmosphere palettes

The Earth-like preset uses the exact daytime color anchors from RFL’s Earthlike atmosphere. This gradient is a palette preview; the game also changes its shading with density, viewing angle, sunlight, twilight and night.

Other atmosphere categories follow the theme of the Elite Dangerous atmosphere reference. Their palettes are artistic approximations, not verified game color mappings. Noble-gas colors here are artistic choices, not emission colors or predictions from gas identity alone.

Planet and atmosphere choices update this preview immediately. Cool, temperate and warm rocky worlds with the nitrogen-rich preset also configure the browser climate model. Extreme worlds with supported atmospheres use a separately labeled surface estimate. Remaining combinations are appearance previews.
